svg.text: Job monitor | From public posting to action
Current design: one Python process on an Oracle Ubuntu VM, checking 24 public boards.
systemd supervises the worker: restart on failure; boot startup configured.
Webhook URL stays on the VM
Solid arrows: job/results flow. Dashed arrows: configuration and visibility.
One new job | Where time is spent
A 60-second poll interval is one part of the journey; it is not an end-to-end delivery guarantee.
UNMEASURED: original publication to a visible phone notification
Why this is appropriate for one person
Adapter pattern: each job provider becomes the same job format.
Single writer: one coordinator owns history; workers do network I/O.
Persistent outbox: save leads before sending; retry independently.
Bounded concurrency: four fetches and one sender keep load controlled.
At-least-once delivery: ambiguous acknowledgement can cause a duplicate.
A supervised process and local files keep the system small.
What we still need to validate
Coverage: compare the selected feeds with employers’ career pages.
Screening: expose rejection reasons and review missed matches.
Speed: observe naturally discovered jobs and their measured delays.
Freshness: last publication / record creation are not first publication.
Reliability: verify recovery, off-VM history backup and outage visibility.
Historical health: 24/24 boards healthy at the last user-shared check.
Architecture reflects the repository on 2026-10-13. Latest health is historical evidence, not a live dashboard.
